headline: A 2013 House resolution that was voted down would have expressed the House's wish that conference negotiators drop limits on the USDA's sugar import quota authority.
what_it_does: This was a nonbinding sense-of-the-House resolution, so it would not have changed any law by itself. It would have told the House managers in conference on H.R. 2642, the farm bill, to push for repealing the 2008 law language that governs how tariff-rate quotas for raw and refined sugar are administered. If that repeal had been adopted, the Secretary of Agriculture would have regained authority to manage sugar supplies to meet domestic demand at reasonable prices.

who_it_affects.how: The department would have regained authority over how sugar supplies are managed through tariff-rate quotas, if the repeal were later enacted.
Their market conditions could have been affected by changes to how USDA manages sugar import quotas.
Retail sugar prices could have been affected by the USDA's management of domestic sugar supply.
